subject.title: [Feature]: Support configurable request labels for Gemini API calls (GCP billing tracking)

question: Should OpenClaw expose configurable Google Vertex request labels as public provider config, and what schema, provider scope, and privacy/cardinality limits should it use?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but choosing a permanent billing metadata contract affects public config, provider ownership, privacy, and Vertex versus non-Vertex behavior.

options.title: Approve bounded Vertex labels
options.body: Expose a validated Google/Vertex label map in the Google plugin, limit it to Vertex-supported requests, and document GCP label constraints and safe metadata guidance.

options.title: Decline first-class labels
options.body: Keep core/provider config unchanged and document that operators must use external proxying or GCP-side project separation when billing labels are required.

options.title: Defer for cross-provider metadata design
options.body: Keep this as product backlog until OpenClaw has a broader request-metadata design across provider-specific billing and attribution surfaces.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded Vertex labels
recommendation.body: Expose a validated Google/Vertex label map in the Google plugin, limit it to Vertex-supported requests, and document GCP label constraints and safe metadata guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses provider config and Google runtime ownership, and this handle has the strongest recent config/provider routing history among the identified owners.
